lanes.title: entering a battle costs morale (D-083 DB1), reference annex rebuilt from the research dossier, lane MOR's open round-2 items
lanes.brief: SCOPE LIMITS: work only in prototypes/m7-sprint1 (M7Proto.slnx; M7Econ.slnx only if economy code is touched) and docs/m7-plan; no change to Sim.Core, Sim.Data, Sim.Cli, Sim.Ui or their tests, no unit data or cap change, no permanent project, no CI change (D-079 §6, Q5 open). Every design document is marked PROPOSAL; every reading is labelled READING with both alternatives; no Director decision is invented or reopened. Read docs/d083-entering-battle-costs-morale-2026-11-10.md in full first (DB1, DB2, the readings DB1-R1..R3, §3 supersessions, §4 delegated, §5), then docs/d082-morale-caps-ties-director-answers-2026-11-10.md, then lane MOR's docs/m7-plan/morale-proposal.md and prototypes/m7-sprint1/reports/H-MOR.md (every section, including the verification rounds §10 and §11), and lane AP's reports/H-AP.md and docs/m7-plan/concealment-actions-proposal.md. Research input: the provenance-checked dossier /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7c/research/run1/dossier.md (claim files official.json, data.json, community.json, targeted.json; verdicts check.json; hosts hosts.json; the schema copies under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7c/research/run1/work-data/notes/) with its claim files and check.json (a separate research pass; do not redo it; cite its claim ids). Read first in the dossier: the answers to Q1 and Q2, the MOR2-input section and the genre row G. In short (the dossier is the authority): the reference's data defines no morale key for entering a battle, deploying or time in battle (CODE, definitions only, no values); it defines an inherited 36-key army-morale family on the campaign map (a win bonus that falls off with the armies' relative strength and lasts some turns, a loss penalty, a casualty multiplier, idle, foreign soil, attrition and others) whose use in the reference is unknown; a sibling title's auto-resolve has a minimum morale loss per combat round that the reference lacks (CODE, sibling); and a genre game charges deployed troops a daily morale cost (WEAK). Use these as reference only (D-069). (1) ENTRY COST (D-083 DB1). Design it in morale-proposal.md (a new section, PROPOSAL; mark superseded statements in place, struck with a dated bold note, as lane MOR did): the cost a formation pays for entering a battle, once per battle (DB1-R2 (a)), when it is placed on the field: at the start, in its deployment third, or at its arrival as a reinforcement (DB1-R1 (a)); a formation that never reaches the field pays nothing. It combines with DR29's decrease and DA1's rise as separate terms (DB1-R3 (a)): a lossless win nets rise minus cost, which can be negative after beating a small force (say for which force ratios with the proposed numbers), and a lossless loss costs the cost. Where it is charged is delegated (D-083 §4): analyse (i) in the battle at the entry instant (in both resolvers, or in the campaign-to-battle hand-off for battles started from the campaign), (ii) only in the after-battle settlement, (iii) both. The in-battle recovery (HoldRecovery, RallyRecovery) can make up a cost taken only from the start morale, so lane D's net-loss settlement (start - end - restore, floored at 0) would carry none of it: the design must make the cost reach the army's campaign morale EXACTLY whatever the battle does (for example a separate settlement term recorded on the settlement row), and say whether the battle itself feels it. Propose the size with its reasoning (D-082 §5 delegates every number; relate it to DA1's rise, MoraleMax and the rout threshold), citing the dossier where it supports or contradicts the design. Law 2 (an event cost on a stock, not a buff), Law 3 (an event, not a rate; any rate part integrates with dtYears), Law 5 (integer micro units, no float). Lane D's War Sandbox: say how its Quick Battle charges the cost. (2) PROTOTYPE: implement the entry cost where the design puts it, plus the settlement term; keep lane MOR's DA1 rise, DR29's decrease, the baseline and the 'fight it won' rule as they are (its default stays 0). Tests: the cost is charged exactly once per formation per battle (a formation that withdraws and re-enters pays once); a reinforcement pays at its arrival instant, turn-exact (a pin that fails if it pays at the battle's start or one step late); a lossless win nets rise minus cost exactly; a lossless loss costs exactly the cost; the cost reaches the campaign morale exactly even when the in-battle recovery makes up the start loss; a formation that never reaches the field pays nothing; the clamp at 0; tie-dense ordering where several armies settle at one instant; POPULATED-table round-trip tests for any changed or new serialized row (ExpectedLength, bit-exact round trip, hash equality; bump the codec version if a row changes); lane AP's equal-sides and ambush morale tests updated with the cost, each change attributed. If either resolver changes, measure lane P's tuning battery off and on (digests, outcome and winner changes, rule P1), and give every moved golden or pin a measured attribution; lane P's acceptance stays OPEN (D-079 Q4). (2b) THE MUTUAL-ELIMINATION WIN (lane AP's observation AP-R1-14, H-AP §9): under DA6 a defender whose battle formations were all eliminated in the same instant as the attacker's (BothEliminated) is the reported winner, and DA1 then raises its army's morale (MEASURED by lane AP: 900,000 against 700,000). Say whether DA1's rise should depend on what the winner has left (for example scale B or the rise by the winner's surviving share), as a PROPOSAL with its alternative; implement it only if the design adopts it, with tests. (3) LANE MOR's OPEN ROUND-2 ITEMS: MOR-V2-04 (a test for the AutoResolver's in-contact volley record in the hit table; the verifier's mutant H1 must die); the zero-damage guard in both damage paths (mutants G3 and L1 of H-MOR §11.6 must each die by a semantic test, or be argued equivalent with a measurement); MOR-V2-05 (the three 'Pattern seen' cells of the proposal's later-mechanisms table that cite annex sections without the pattern: rout contagion, fatigue, missile fire). (4) ANNEX A REWRITE: rebuild the morale proposal's Annex A from the dossier, keeping lane MOR's labels and adding the dossier's FETCH label where it applies, each row with its claim id and check verdict; earlier rows the dossier did not re-establish stay only struck or marked WEAK, never as fact; nothing of the reference's names, numbers or text enters our design (D-069). (5) Lane report prototypes/m7-sprint1/reports/H-MOR2.md (what exists, design, readings applied, decisions for the Director only where genuinely undecided, MEASURED vs INFERRED, tests, mutants, what ran, NOT RUN, deferred). Builds and tests: M7Proto.slnx Debug and Release, prototypes/m7-sprint1/scripts/check-proto-determinism.sh, python3 scripts/check-doc-links.py --all.
